ME-2024-LD549.policyArea: CRIMINAL PROCEDURE, EVIDENCE, FORENSIC EXAMINATION KITS
ME-2024-LD549.aiSummary: The bill would set up a statewide system to track sexual assault forensic exam kits and would require state agencies, hospitals, labs, police, and district attorneys to use it. It would also change how long kits are stored, require many kits to be sent to the Maine State Police Crime Laboratory for testing starting January 1, 2027, and give victims anonymous access to track their kit. The bill would also require the state to report on kit counts and testing times each year.

ME-2024-LD534.aiSummary: The bill would require professional investigators to tell crime victims and witnesses why they are asking questions, who their client is, and whether the person may benefit from the work. If a victim, witness, or a minor’s parent or guardian asks them to stop, they could not keep contacting that person unless given permission.

ME-2024-LD527.policyArea: BAIL AND RECOGNIZANCE, BAIL OFFICERS, CRIMINAL PROCEDURE
ME-2024-LD527.aiSummary: The bill would create bail officers in the judicial branch to help set and carry out bail under Maine law. It would let bail officers, along with bail commissioners, set preconviction bail in many cases, while keeping limits for murder cases, some serious crimes, and domestic violence cases. It would also set training rules and allow a bail commissioner fee of up to $60, with exceptions for people who cannot pay.

ME-2024-LD2066.policyArea: AFFORDABILITY PROGRAM, CHILD CARE, CHILDREN AND FAMILIES
ME-2024-LD2066.aiSummary: The bill would create the Child Care Employment Award, a state program that gives child care help to workers at licensed child care centers and family child care homes whose own children use licensed care. The help would be paid directly to the care provider, and the Health and Human Services Department could set rules on award amounts, waiting lists, quality standards, and how many children can be helped. It would also add one full-time staff job to run the program and provide $3,000,000 in funding for the 2026-27 year.

ME-2024-LD13.policyArea: ELECTIONS, MATERIALS AND WORKING GROUP, POLLING PLACES
ME-2024-LD13.aiSummary: The bill would create a state fund in the Secretary of State’s office to pay for making and delivering election materials, like ballots, absentee ballot envelopes, and voter forms. It would move $266,000 from the state’s general surplus each year starting in 2025, with that amount adjusted every two years for cost of living. It would also bring back a working group to study schools used as polling places and have the department report its findings and recommendations by December 15, 2025.

ME-2024-LD1252.aiSummary: The bill would change the rules for the Maine Agriculture, Food System and Forest Products Infrastructure Investment Advisory Board and the fund it oversees. It would limit grants to producers that have, or are trying to build, a processing or manufacturing facility in Maine, and would require the money to support that facility and related equipment or supply chain needs. It would also bar board members from voting on a matter when they have a conflict of interest, meaning a direct personal financial stake for themselves or an immediate family member.

ME-2024-LD1061.aiSummary: The bill would give $1,563,470 from the General Fund each year in 2025-26 and 2026-27 to the Department of Health and Human Services. ME-2024-LD1043.policyArea: PUBLIC LANDS, STATE PARKS, VETERANS AND MILITARY PERSONNEL
ME-2024-LD1043.aiSummary: The bill would let the state give free day-use passes to state parks and historic sites to the immediate family members of qualifying veterans and active duty military members. It would allow spouses, domestic partners, and dependent children to have their own passes. The passes would be for admission to state parks and historic sites.
